title: Lantern Orbit (subscriber paywall)
charter:
# Project Charter: Lantern Orbit
Domain: Media and Entertainment. Business unit: Content Operations. Initiative type: regulatory module.
## Purpose
The purpose of Lantern Orbit is to introduce controls in the subscriber paywall that close audit findings.
## Background
The deadline is immovable because it is tied to a regulatory effective date. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Objectives
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the subscriber paywall.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Reduce average handling time for subscribers by 37 percent.
## Scope
In scope: the subscriber paywall and the processes used by subscribers.
Out of scope: Organisational restructuring of the operations teams. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 12 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 36 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Content Operations. Lessons learned from previous initiatives in this area have been reviewed.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Small increments will be shipped daily and measured in production. Customer identity and financial data flow through the service. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of PCI DSS v4.0.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP00001: Lantern Orbit (subscriber paywall).
Workflow archetype adopted: Scaled Agile Release Train. State flow: Programme Backlog > Feature Analysis > Committed to Increment > Feature In Progress > System Demo > Integration Testing > Release Ready > Released.
Workflow adjustments applied: add accessibility review, add security review.
Outcome score 0.70 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 81%, defect escape rate 7.0%, median cycle time 6.5 days, stakeholder satisfaction 3.8 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.
The team adapted the lifecycle informally because parts of it did not fit the work.
Charter summary follows.

title: Northern Waypoint (virtual ward platform)
charter:
# Project Charter: Northern Waypoint
Domain: Healthcare Provision. Business unit: Clinical Systems.
## Purpose
The purpose of Northern Waypoint is to keep the virtual ward platform secure, patched and performant while reducing the defect backlog.
## Background
Roughly 37 percent of team capacity is consumed by unplanned tickets and urgent fixes. Documentation will be maintained in the shared knowledge space.
## Objectives
* Reduce average handling time for general practitioners by 19 percent.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.2 out of 5.
## Scope
In scope: the virtual ward platform and the processes used by general practitioners.
Out of scope: Replacement of the finance general ledger. Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 8 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 43 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Clinical Systems. Success will be measured against the benefits profile in the business case.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Changes to production must respect the quarterly change freeze and the weekly change advisory board. Training for end users will be coordinated with the change management team.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018.

Outcome score 0.48 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 49%, defect escape rate 10.5%, median cycle time 9.9 days, stakeholder satisfaction 2.8 out of 5, 2 compliance findings.
Process friction was the most common theme in retrospectives.
Charter summary follows.

Domain: Pharmaceuticals and Life Sciences. Business unit: Pharmacovigilance.
## Purpose
The purpose of Tidal Tributary is to integrate the laboratory data capture service with a commercial off the shelf package.
## Background
Delivery depends on milestones from our technology partner. The product owner has authority to make day to day scope decisions within agreed tolerances.

* Cut operational cost of the laboratory data capture service by 17 percent.
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.7 out of 5.
* Reduce defect escape rate by 37 percent compared with the previous release.

In scope: the laboratory data capture service and the processes used by pharmacovigilance scientists.
Out of scope: Organisational restructuring of the operations teams. Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts.
## Team and Stakeholders
The planned duration is 39 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Pharmacovigilance. The project will report progress to the portfolio board each month.
## Constraints and Assumptions
The team will share a dashboard of delivery metrics with sponsors.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. Controls required under ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls apply to this service.

title: Vantage Ledger (admissions decision workflow)
charter:
# Project Charter: Vantage Ledger
Domain: Education. Business unit: Student Services.
## Purpose
The purpose of Vantage Ledger is to coordinate a programme that rebuilds the admissions decision workflow across several product teams.
## Background
The system will store personal data including names, contact details and account history. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Objectives
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.3 out of 5.
* Cut operational cost of the admissions decision workflow by 32 percent.
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the admissions decision workflow.
## Scope
In scope: the admissions decision workflow and the processes used by lecturers.
Out of scope: Changes to the enterprise identity provider. Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 118 people organised into 7 teams. The planned duration is 70 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Student Services. The team is co located three days a week and remote on other days.
## Constraints and Assumptions
The core scope is understood although some secondary features remain open. The product owner has authority to make day to day scope decisions within agreed tolerances.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. The solution falls within scope of ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls. Compliance with WCAG 2.2 AA and the Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations must be demonstrated before go live.

Workflow adjustments applied: add accessibility review, add dependency sync, add security review, add stakeholder demo.
Outcome score 0.99 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 90%, defect escape rate 1.6%, median cycle time 4.3 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.8 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.
The lifecycle suited the problem; ceremonies and gates felt proportionate rather than bureaucratic.

title: Atlas Quarry (student enrolment portal)
charter:
# Project Charter: Atlas Quarry
Domain: Education. Business unit: Learning Technology.
## Purpose
The purpose of Atlas Quarry is to give admissions officers a self service student enrolment portal to replace email requests.
## Background
Changes after tooling is cut are extremely expensive, so design decisions must be frozen early. Architecture decisions will be recorded and reviewed by the design authority.
## Objectives
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.4 out of 5.
* Increase digital adoption among admissions officers to 43 percent within a year.
* Retire 4 legacy components by the end of the project.
## Scope
In scope: the student enrolment portal and the processes used by admissions officers.
Out of scope: Organisational restructuring of the operations teams. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 4 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 24 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Learning Technology. Lessons learned from previous initiatives in this area have been reviewed.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Historical data must be reconciled and migrated before the old system is switched off. Around 24 percent of capacity will go to support requests alongside planned roadmap work. Funding beyond the first phase depends on demonstrated benefits.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. The solution falls within scope of WCAG 2.2 AA and the Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations.
text:

Workflow archetype adopted: Scrumban Hybrid Flow. State flow: Backlog > Ready > In Progress > Review > Testing > Done.
Workflow adjustments applied: add uat stage.
Outcome score 0.76 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 83%, defect escape rate 5.9%, median cycle time 6.1 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.0 out of 5, 1 compliance findings.
The chosen workflow matched the nature of the work and the team settled into a steady rhythm.
Charter summary follows.

charter:

Domain: Manufacturing. Business unit: Product Engineering.
## Purpose
The purpose of Quiet Cascade is to build the first release of a production scheduling engine for line supervisors.
## Background
Two suppliers deliver modules that must be accepted against contractual criteria. The project will report progress to the portfolio board each month.
## Objectives
* Increase digital adoption among line supervisors to 34 percent within a year.
* Cut operational cost of the production scheduling engine by 15 percent.

Out of scope: Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed. Replacement of the finance general ledger.

The team deploys to production several times per day behind feature flags. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.

Controls required under the NIS2 Directive apply to this service.

title: Copper Quarry (asset condition monitoring)
charter:
# Project Charter: Copper Quarry
Domain: Energy and Utilities. Business unit: Smart Metering.
## Purpose
The purpose of Copper Quarry is to prototype predictive models that could power the asset condition monitoring.
## Background
We must establish quickly whether the approach works before committing to a full build. Lessons learned from previous initiatives in this area have been reviewed.
## Objectives
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Increase digital adoption among asset managers to 27 percent within a year.
* Reduce average handling time for asset managers by 21 percent.
## Scope
In scope: the asset condition monitoring and the processes used by asset managers.
Out of scope: Replacement of the finance general ledger. Native tablet applications.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 6 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 20 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Smart Metering. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Requirements are expected to evolve as we learn from early customer feedback. Customer identity and financial data flow through the service. The project will report progress to the portfolio board each month.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Controls required under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to this service. Compliance with ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls must be demonstrated before go live.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP00011: Copper Quarry (asset condition monitoring).
Workflow archetype adopted: Dual Track Discovery and Delivery. State flow: Opportunity Backlog > Hypothesis Framing > Discovery Research > Experiment Running > Evidence Review > Delivery Backlog > Building > Validation in Production > Learned and Shipped.
Workflow adjustments applied: add definition of ready, add model validation, add security review, add spike timebox.
Outcome score 0.86 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 84%, defect escape rate 4.8%, median cycle time 5.1 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.1 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.
The chosen workflow matched the nature of the work and the team settled into a steady rhythm.
Charter summary follows.

title: Summit Bridge (billing engine)
charter:
# Project Charter: Summit Bridge
Domain: Energy and Utilities. Business unit: Grid Operations. Initiative type: infrastructure upgrade.
## Purpose
The purpose of Summit Bridge is to upgrade the infrastructure behind the billing engine to supported versions.
## Background
Customer identity and financial data flow through the service. An external vendor supplies a core component under a fixed price contract. Success will be measured against the benefits profile in the business case.
## Objectives
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Cut operational cost of the billing engine by 41 percent.
* Reduce defect escape rate by 10 percent compared with the previous release.
## Scope
In scope: the billing engine and the processes used by field engineers.
Out of scope: Changes to the enterprise identity provider. Organisational restructuring of the operations teams.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 5 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 24 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Grid Operations. Lessons learned from previous initiatives in this area have been reviewed.
## Constraints and Assumptions
The platform is classified as a critical service with a recovery time objective of 120 minutes. Roughly 34 percent of team capacity is consumed by unplanned tickets and urgent fixes. The project will report progress to the portfolio board each month.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Compliance with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 must be demonstrated before go live. The solution falls within scope of ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls. Controls required under Sarbanes Oxley Section 404 internal controls apply to this service.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP00012: Summit Bridge (billing engine).
Workflow archetype adopted: Change Controlled Operations. State flow: Change Request > Risk Assessment > Change Advisory Board Review > Scheduled > Implementing > Post Implementation Review > Closed.
Workflow adjustments applied: add data migration rehearsal, add privacy review, add security review, add vendor checkpoint, tighten wip.
Outcome score 0.88 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 88%, defect escape rate 5.3%, median cycle time 6.8 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.6 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.
The lifecycle suited the problem; ceremonies and gates felt proportionate rather than bureaucratic.
Charter summary follows.

title: Riverside Sentinel (remote monitoring dashboard)
charter:
# Project Charter: Riverside Sentinel
Domain: Healthcare Provision. Business unit: Patient Services. Initiative type: customer facing application.
## Purpose
The purpose of Riverside Sentinel is to rebuild the remote monitoring dashboard as a mobile first experience for patients.
## Background
Sensitive personal information will be processed and retained under our data policy. The team will balance roadmap items with a moderate volume of operational requests. The sponsor anticipates frequent reprioritisation as the market position becomes clearer. The product owner has authority to make day to day scope decisions within agreed tolerances.
## Objectives
* Increase digital adoption among patients to 19 percent within a year.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the remote monitoring dashboard.
## Scope
In scope: the remote monitoring dashboard and the processes used by patients.
Out of scope: Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed. Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 6 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 19 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Patient Services. The team is co located three days a week and remote on other days.
## Constraints and Assumptions
The team deploys to production several times per day behind feature flags. Several business owners share accountability for outcomes. This is a public channel and must work for people with a wide range of needs. Little change is expected because the functional design was agreed in detail with all parties. Architecture decisions will be recorded and reviewed by the design authority.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules. The solution falls within scope of WCAG 2.2 AA and the Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations.
text:

Workflow archetype adopted: Scrumban Hybrid Flow. State flow: Backlog > Ready > In Progress > Review > Testing > Done.
Workflow adjustments applied: add definition of ready, add privacy review, add security review.
Outcome score 0.59 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 67%, defect escape rate 8.6%, median cycle time 11.2 days, stakeholder satisfaction 3.3 out of 5, 2 compliance findings.
Predictability was acceptable, but the process needed several mid course corrections.
Charter summary follows.

charter:
# Project Charter: Beacon Canopy
Domain: Medical Devices. Business unit: Post Market Surveillance.
## Purpose
The purpose of Beacon Canopy is to build the first release of a wearable cardiac monitor app for clinicians.
## Background
This is a public channel and must work for people with a wide range of needs. The work includes migrating approximately 29 million records from the legacy platform. Sensitive personal information will be processed and retained under our data policy. An external vendor supplies a core component under a fixed price contract. The team will share a dashboard of delivery metrics with sponsors.
## Objectives
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.4 out of 5.
* Reduce defect escape rate by 25 percent compared with the previous release.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
## Scope
In scope: the wearable cardiac monitor app and the processes used by clinicians.
Out of scope: Changes to the enterprise identity provider. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 7 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 20 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Post Market Surveillance. Training for end users will be coordinated with the change management team.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Requirements are stable and fully specified in the approved requirements catalogue. Peak load is forecast at 1600 requests per second during seasonal campaigns. A machine learning model will score cases and route them to the right queue. All changes require an approved implementation plan and a defined change window. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of IEC 62304 medical device software lifecycle. Compliance with ISO 13485 quality management system must be demonstrated before go live.

Outcome score 0.24 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 39%, defect escape rate 14.8%, median cycle time 14.1 days, stakeholder satisfaction 2.4 out of 5, 4 compliance findings.

Charter summary follows.

Domain: Telecommunications. Business unit: Consumer Mobile. Initiative type: hardware and firmware.
## Purpose
The purpose of Linden Canopy is to deliver a firmware release for the core network software upgrade that ships with the next hardware revision.
## Background
Scope has been contractually fixed and signed off by the steering committee. Any downtime breaches contractual service levels and triggers financial penalties. Success will be measured against the benefits profile in the business case.
## Objectives
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Cut operational cost of the core network software upgrade by 26 percent.
* Increase digital adoption among retail advisors to 12 percent within a year.
## Scope
In scope: the core network software upgrade and the processes used by retail advisors.
Out of scope: Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed. Native tablet applications.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 12 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 68 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Consumer Mobile. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Hardware prototypes arrive in batches, constraining when integration testing can start. Two suppliers deliver modules that must be accepted against contractual criteria. Acceptance by the commissioning client is a contractual requirement. The project will report progress to the portfolio board each month.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP00070: Linden Canopy (core network software upgrade).
Workflow archetype adopted: Stage Gate Phased Delivery. State flow: Initiation > Requirements Definition > Solution Design > Build > System Testing > Deployment Readiness > Closed.
Workflow adjustments applied: add accessibility review, add feature flags, add rollback plan, add security review, add stakeholder demo.
Outcome score 0.71 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 77%, defect escape rate 7.4%, median cycle time 6.9 days, stakeholder satisfaction 3.7 out of 5, 1 compliance findings.
The lifecycle suited the problem; ceremonies and gates felt proportionate rather than bureaucratic.
Charter summary follows.

title: Coastal Cascade (customer self care app)
charter:
# Project Charter: Coastal Cascade
Domain: Telecommunications. Business unit: OSS and BSS.
## Purpose
The purpose of Coastal Cascade is to sustain the customer self care app for network operations engineers with predictable response times for fixes.
## Background
Several business owners share accountability for outcomes. Sensitive personal information will be processed and retained under our data policy. The team deploys to production several times per day behind feature flags. The product owner has authority to make day to day scope decisions within agreed tolerances.
## Objectives
* Retire 4 legacy components by the end of the project.
* Cut operational cost of the customer self care app by 11 percent.
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the customer self care app.
## Scope
In scope: the customer self care app and the processes used by network operations engineers.
Out of scope: Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The planned duration is 38 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within OSS and BSS. Budget has been approved for the current financial year.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Roughly 30 percent of team capacity is consumed by unplanned tickets and urgent fixes. Previous infrastructure changes caused two major incidents, so change control is under scrutiny. Integration points with enterprise platforms must be coordinated across several teams. Training for end users will be coordinated with the change management team.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. Compliance with ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls must be demonstrated before go live. Controls required under the NIS2 Directive apply to this service.

Outcome score 0.89 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 93%, defect escape rate 4.7%, median cycle time 4.2 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.8 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.
The lifecycle suited the problem; ceremonies and gates felt proportionate rather than bureaucratic.
Charter summary follows.

title: Coastal Mosaic (stability study tracker)
charter:
# Project Charter: Coastal Mosaic
Domain: Pharmaceuticals and Life Sciences. Business unit: Clinical Operations. Initiative type: machine learning research.
## Purpose
The purpose of Coastal Mosaic is to establish whether machine learning can improve decisions in the stability study tracker.
## Background
Sensitive personal information will be processed and retained under our data policy. Predictions will be generated by a trained model that must be monitored for drift. Training for end users will be coordinated with the change management team.
## Objectives
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.6 out of 5.
* Increase digital adoption among trial sites to 24 percent within a year.
## Scope
In scope: the stability study tracker and the processes used by trial sites.
Out of scope: Native tablet applications. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 5 people organised into 1 team. The sponsor sits within Clinical Operations. Budget has been approved for the current financial year.
## Constraints and Assumptions
We must establish quickly whether the approach works before committing to a full build. We do not yet know which capabilities will matter most, so the scope will be shaped by usage data. Key risks will be tracked in the project risk register.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Compliance with FDA 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records and signatures must be demonstrated before go live.

Workflow adjustments applied: add spike timebox.
Outcome score 0.33 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 45%, defect escape rate 13.2%, median cycle time 12.4 days, stakeholder satisfaction 2.5 out of 5, 4 compliance findings.

The purpose of Summit Cascade is to modernise the device telemetry gateway estate through a coordinated portfolio of teams.

The service will be used directly by members of the public. Sensitive personal information will be processed and retained under our data policy. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.

The purpose of Atlas Prism is to coordinate a programme that rebuilds the benefits eligibility checker across several product teams.

A machine learning model will score cases and route them to the right queue. Delivery spans 6 teams across 3 locations with shared release dependencies. Changes after tooling is cut are extremely expensive, so design decisions must be frozen early. Delivery depends on milestones from our technology partner. # Project Charter: Silver Beacon
Domain: Financial Services. Business unit: Treasury Operations. Initiative type: new product feature.
## Purpose
The purpose of Silver Beacon is to build the first release of a mortgage origination journey for traders.
## Background
Traffic spikes sharply at month end and during marketing events. The system will store personal data including names, contact details and account history. The roadmap is broadly agreed but individual items will be refined as they approach delivery. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.
## Objectives
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the mortgage origination journey.
* Retire 6 legacy components by the end of the project.
* Reduce defect escape rate by 21 percent compared with the previous release.
## Scope
In scope: the mortgage origination journey and the processes used by traders.
Out of scope: Native tablet applications. Organisational restructuring of the operations teams.

The delivery team comprises 8 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 26 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Treasury Operations. Lessons learned from previous initiatives in this area have been reviewed.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Acceptance by the commissioning client is a contractual requirement. The team deploys to production several times per day behind feature flags. This is a public channel and must work for people with a wide range of needs. Requirements are expected to evolve as we learn from early customer feedback. Documentation will be maintained in the shared knowledge space.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Compliance with MiFID II record keeping obligations must be demonstrated before go live.

# Project Charter: Quiet Vector
Domain: Insurance. Business unit: Broker Channels. Initiative type: infrastructure upgrade.
## Purpose
The purpose of Quiet Vector is to harden the network and compute estate supporting the broker quotation portal.
## Background
Peak load is forecast at 7200 requests per second during seasonal campaigns. Small increments will be shipped daily and measured in production. Requirements are stable and fully specified in the approved requirements catalogue. An external vendor supplies a core component under a fixed price contract. Lessons learned from previous initiatives in this area have been reviewed.
## Objectives
* Reduce defect escape rate by 20 percent compared with the previous release.
* Increase digital adoption among brokers to 12 percent within a year.
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the broker quotation portal.
## Scope
In scope: the broker quotation portal and the processes used by brokers.
Out of scope: Replacement of the finance general ledger. Native tablet applications.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 5 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 28 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Broker Channels. Budget has been approved for the current financial year.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Any downtime breaches contractual service levels and triggers financial penalties. Around 30 percent of capacity will go to support requests alongside planned roadmap work. All changes require an approved implementation plan and a defined change window. Predictions will be generated by a trained model that must be monitored for drift. Funding beyond the first phase depends on demonstrated benefits.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of the FCA Consumer Duty. Controls required under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to this service. The solution falls within scope of Sarbanes Oxley Section 404 internal controls.

## Purpose
The purpose of Granite Signal is to coordinate a programme that rebuilds the court booking system across several product teams.

Sensitive personal information will be processed and retained under our data policy. Cross team dependencies are the primary schedule risk identified by the programme office. The product owner has authority to make day to day scope decisions within agreed tolerances.

* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the court booking system.

Out of scope: Organisational restructuring of the operations teams. Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed.

# Project Charter: Sterling Current
Domain: Education. Business unit: Learning Technology.
## Purpose
The purpose of Sterling Current is to stabilise the timetabling service and work down accumulated technical debt.
## Background
The team handles a steady stream of incidents and service requests that arrive without notice. Lessons learned from previous initiatives in this area have been reviewed.
## Objectives
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the timetabling service.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Cut operational cost of the timetabling service by 23 percent.
## Scope
In scope: the timetabling service and the processes used by admissions officers.
Out of scope: Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 4 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 29 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Learning Technology. Budget has been approved for the current financial year.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Around 42 percent of capacity will go to support requests alongside planned roadmap work. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of WCAG 2.2 AA and the Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP00317: Sterling Current (timetabling service).
Workflow archetype adopted: Agile Scrum Product Delivery. State flow: Product Backlog > Sprint Backlog > In Progress > Code Review > QA Verification > Ready for Release > Done.
Workflow adjustments applied: add accessibility review, add model validation, tighten wip.
Outcome score 0.51 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 68%, defect escape rate 10.4%, median cycle time 9.8 days, stakeholder satisfaction 3.1 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.
The lifecycle created waiting time and hand offs that did not add value.
Charter summary follows.

title: Juniper Prism (supplier portal)
charter:
# Project Charter: Juniper Prism
Domain: Manufacturing. Business unit: Plant Systems.
## Purpose
The purpose of Juniper Prism is to absorb incoming service requests and incidents for the supplier portal.
## Background
Any downtime breaches contractual service levels and triggers financial penalties. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Objectives
* Reduce defect escape rate by 26 percent compared with the previous release.
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the supplier portal.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
## Scope
In scope: the supplier portal and the processes used by line supervisors.
Out of scope: Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed. Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 9 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 43 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Plant Systems. Budget has been approved for the current financial year.
## Constraints and Assumptions
A broad stakeholder group must stay informed, including executive sponsors and frontline managers. Demand is interrupt driven, with priority one incidents expected to be picked up within the hour. Training for end users will be coordinated with the change management team.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
There are no sector specific regulatory requirements for this work.
text:

Workflow archetype adopted: Agile Scrum Product Delivery. State flow: Product Backlog > Sprint Backlog > In Progress > Code Review > QA Verification > Ready for Release > Done.
Workflow adjustments applied: add rollback plan, add stakeholder demo, tighten wip.
Outcome score 0.71 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 76%, defect escape rate 6.5%, median cycle time 7.4 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.0 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.
Predictability was acceptable, but the process needed several mid course corrections.
Charter summary follows.

title: Cobalt Sentinel (card controls feature)
charter:
# Project Charter: Cobalt Sentinel
Domain: Financial Services. Business unit: Retail Banking. Initiative type: regulatory module.
## Purpose
The purpose of Cobalt Sentinel is to deliver the card controls feature required to demonstrate compliance to the regulator.
## Background
Little change is expected because the functional design was agreed in detail with all parties. Budget has been approved for the current financial year.
## Objectives
* Retire 4 legacy components by the end of the project.
* Cut operational cost of the card controls feature by 33 percent.
* Reduce average handling time for retail customers by 20 percent.
## Scope
In scope: the card controls feature and the processes used by retail customers.
Out of scope: Replacement of the finance general ledger. Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 9 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 24 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Retail Banking. The product owner has authority to make day to day scope decisions within agreed tolerances.
## Constraints and Assumptions
A fixed go live date of February 2025 has been set by an external obligation. A broad stakeholder group must stay informed, including executive sponsors and frontline managers. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of the FCA Consumer Duty. Compliance with ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls must be demonstrated before go live. Controls required under MiFID II record keeping obligations apply to this service.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP00319: Cobalt Sentinel (card controls feature).
Workflow archetype adopted: Regulated Compliance Pipeline. State flow: Draft Requirement > Requirements Traceability > Design Review > Implementation > Verification > Independent Validation > Compliance Review > Release Authorisation > Released.
Workflow adjustments applied: add stakeholder demo.
Outcome score 0.67 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 74%, defect escape rate 10.1%, median cycle time 8.6 days, stakeholder satisfaction 3.7 out of 5, 1 compliance findings.
Flow through the workflow was smooth and predictable for most of the project.
Charter summary follows.

title: Tidal Mosaic (assessment marking tool)
charter:
# Project Charter: Tidal Mosaic
Domain: Education. Business unit: Learning Technology.
## Purpose
The purpose of Tidal Mosaic is to rebuild the assessment marking tool as a mobile first experience for researchers.
## Background
Little change is expected because the functional design was agreed in detail with all parties. We release continuously through an automated pipeline with progressive rollout. Documentation will be maintained in the shared knowledge space.
## Objectives
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Increase digital adoption among researchers to 32 percent within a year.
* Reduce average handling time for researchers by 22 percent.
## Scope
In scope: the assessment marking tool and the processes used by researchers.
Out of scope: Native tablet applications. Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 6 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 23 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Learning Technology. Architecture decisions will be recorded and reviewed by the design authority.
## Constraints and Assumptions
The service will be used directly by members of the public. Firmware must be validated on physical devices before field deployment. Key risks will be tracked in the project risk register.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. Compliance with WCAG 2.2 AA and the Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations must be demonstrated before go live.

Workflow adjustments applied: add feature flags, add performance test, add privacy review.
Outcome score 0.87 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 80%, defect escape rate 4.3%, median cycle time 4.3 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.4 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.

title: Northern Signal (diagnostic imaging viewer)
charter:
# Project Charter: Northern Signal
Domain: Medical Devices. Business unit: Connected Devices. Initiative type: machine learning research.
## Purpose
The purpose of Northern Signal is to investigate data driven approaches to automate the diagnostic imaging viewer.
## Background
Predictions will be generated by a trained model that must be monitored for drift. Key risks will be tracked in the project risk register.
## Objectives
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.4 out of 5.
* Cut operational cost of the diagnostic imaging viewer by 27 percent.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
## Scope
In scope: the diagnostic imaging viewer and the processes used by hospital biomedical teams.
Out of scope: Native tablet applications. Organisational restructuring of the operations teams.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 5 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 28 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Connected Devices. Lessons learned from previous initiatives in this area have been reviewed.
## Constraints and Assumptions
The system will store personal data including names, contact details and account history. Feasibility is unproven; the first weeks will test several competing hypotheses. The team is co located three days a week and remote on other days.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Compliance with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 must be demonstrated before go live. Compliance with IEC 62304 medical device software lifecycle must be demonstrated before go live. Compliance with ISO 13485 quality management system must be demonstrated before go live.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP00321: Northern Signal (diagnostic imaging viewer).
Workflow archetype adopted: Dual Track Discovery and Delivery. State flow: Opportunity Backlog > Hypothesis Framing > Discovery Research > Experiment Running > Evidence Review > Delivery Backlog > Building > Validation in Production > Learned and Shipped.
Workflow adjustments applied: add model validation, add performance test, add privacy review, add spike timebox.
Outcome score 0.93 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 80%, defect escape rate 3.1%, median cycle time 4.5 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.6 out of 5, 2 compliance findings.
Flow through the workflow was smooth and predictable for most of the project.
Charter summary follows.

title: Lantern Prism (adverse event intake system)
charter:
# Project Charter: Lantern Prism
Domain: Pharmaceuticals and Life Sciences. Business unit: Manufacturing Quality.
## Purpose
The purpose of Lantern Prism is to establish whether machine learning can improve decisions in the adverse event intake system.
## Background
Hardware prototypes arrive in batches, constraining when integration testing can start. Feasibility is unproven; the first weeks will test several competing hypotheses. Architecture decisions will be recorded and reviewed by the design authority.
## Objectives
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.0 out of 5.
* Reduce average handling time for clinical research associates by 44 percent.
* Increase digital adoption among clinical research associates to 42 percent within a year.
## Scope
In scope: the adverse event intake system and the processes used by clinical research associates.
Out of scope: Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed. Native tablet applications.
## Team and Stakeholders
The planned duration is 12 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Manufacturing Quality. Key risks will be tracked in the project risk register.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Stakeholders include representatives from 8 departments with differing priorities. The service processes about 750,000 transactions per day and outages have immediate customer impact. Predictions will be generated by a trained model that must be monitored for drift. Lessons learned from previous initiatives in this area have been reviewed.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Controls required under FDA 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records and signatures apply to this service. Compliance with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 must be demonstrated before go live.

Workflow archetype adopted: Dual Track Discovery and Delivery. State flow: Opportunity Backlog > Hypothesis Framing > Discovery Research > Experiment Running > Evidence Review > Delivery Backlog > Building > Validation in Production > Learned and Shipped.
Workflow adjustments applied: add model validation, add spike timebox.
Outcome score 0.80 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 72%, defect escape rate 5.0%, median cycle time 6.2 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.0 out of 5, 1 compliance findings.
The chosen workflow matched the nature of the work and the team settled into a steady rhythm.

Applicable obligations will be confirmed with the compliance team.

# Project Charter: Obsidian Canopy
Domain: Medical Devices. Business unit: Connected Devices.
## Purpose
The purpose of Obsidian Canopy is to deliver an integrated infusion pump firmware update that spans multiple business capabilities.

Delivery spans 10 teams across 3 locations with shared release dependencies. An external customer must sign off each release in their own acceptance environment. * Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.1 out of 5.

In scope: the infusion pump firmware update and the processes used by clinicians.
Out of scope: Replacement of the finance general ledger. Changes to the enterprise identity provider.

charter:
# Project Charter: Tidal Meadow
Domain: Manufacturing. Business unit: Product Engineering.
## Purpose
The purpose of Tidal Meadow is to co develop the quality inspection vision system with our hardware partner for field deployment.
## Background
A fixed go live date of January 2027 has been set by an external obligation. Hardware prototypes arrive in batches, constraining when integration testing can start. Success will be measured against the benefits profile in the business case.

* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the quality inspection vision system.
* Reduce average handling time for suppliers by 29 percent.
* Retire 4 legacy components by the end of the project.
## Scope
In scope: the quality inspection vision system and the processes used by suppliers.
Out of scope: Replacement of the finance general ledger. Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed.

The delivery team comprises 11 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 53 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Product Engineering. The product owner has authority to make day to day scope decisions within agreed tolerances.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Little change is expected because the functional design was agreed in detail with all parties. Changes to production must respect the quarterly change freeze and the weekly change advisory board. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls. Controls required under Sarbanes Oxley Section 404 internal controls apply to this service.

## Purpose
The purpose of Riverside Lattice is to modernise the outage management system estate through a coordinated portfolio of teams.

Customer identity and financial data flow through the service. 12 teams, including two platform teams, contribute to the same release. The service must scale to several million sessions on launch day. The team is co located three days a week and remote on other days.

Domain: Education. Business unit: Admissions. Initiative type: new product feature.
## Purpose
The purpose of Northern Gateway is to launch a timetabling service that differentiates our proposition for admissions officers.
## Background
We do not yet know which capabilities will matter most, so the scope will be shaped by usage data. admissions officers will access the service from their own devices without assistance. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.
## Objectives
* Cut operational cost of the timetabling service by 11 percent.
* Reduce defect escape rate by 32 percent compared with the previous release.
* Retire 5 legacy components by the end of the project.
## Scope
In scope: the timetabling service and the processes used by admissions officers.
Out of scope: Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed. Organisational restructuring of the operations teams.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 8 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 19 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Admissions. The team is co located three days a week and remote on other days.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Customer identity and financial data flow through the service. Delivery depends on milestones from our technology partner. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP00544: Northern Gateway (timetabling service).
Workflow archetype adopted: Agile Scrum Product Delivery. State flow: Product Backlog > Sprint Backlog > In Progress > Code Review > QA Verification > Ready for Release > Done.
Workflow adjustments applied: none.
Outcome score 0.76 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 78%, defect escape rate 5.6%, median cycle time 6.4 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.1 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.
Flow through the workflow was smooth and predictable for most of the project.
Charter summary follows.

title: Pioneer Canopy (smart meter data platform)
charter:
# Project Charter: Pioneer Canopy
Domain: Energy and Utilities. Business unit: Smart Metering. Initiative type: hardware and firmware.
## Purpose
The purpose of Pioneer Canopy is to deliver a firmware release for the smart meter data platform that ships with the next hardware revision.
## Background
Little change is expected because the functional design was agreed in detail with all parties. Documentation will be maintained in the shared knowledge space.
## Objectives
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Reduce defect escape rate by 36 percent compared with the previous release.
* Increase digital adoption among field engineers to 41 percent within a year.
## Scope
In scope: the smart meter data platform and the processes used by field engineers.
Out of scope: Native tablet applications. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 12 people organised into 3 teams. The planned duration is 45 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Smart Metering. Training for end users will be coordinated with the change management team.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Changes after tooling is cut are extremely expensive, so design decisions must be frozen early. The platform is classified as a critical service with a recovery time objective of 60 minutes. Budget has been approved for the current financial year.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Controls required under ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls apply to this service.

Outcome score 0.85 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 81%, defect escape rate 4.5%, median cycle time 4.8 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.3 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.
The chosen workflow matched the nature of the work and the team settled into a steady rhythm.
Charter summary follows.

charter:
# Project Charter: Quartz Relay
Domain: Financial Services. Business unit: Markets Technology. Initiative type: customer facing application.
## Purpose
The purpose of Quartz Relay is to rebuild the credit decisioning engine as a mobile first experience for retail customers.
## Background
Customer identity and financial data flow through the service. We release continuously through an automated pipeline with progressive rollout. The roadmap is broadly agreed but individual items will be refined as they approach delivery. Funding beyond the first phase depends on demonstrated benefits.
## Objectives
* Reduce average handling time for retail customers by 32 percent.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Reduce defect escape rate by 37 percent compared with the previous release.
## Scope
In scope: the credit decisioning engine and the processes used by retail customers.
Out of scope: Native tablet applications. Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 6 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 33 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Markets Technology. Key risks will be tracked in the project risk register.
## Constraints and Assumptions
The service will be used directly by members of the public. Several business owners share accountability for outcomes. Integration points with enterprise platforms must be coordinated across several teams. The product owner has authority to make day to day scope decisions within agreed tolerances.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Controls required under the FCA Consumer Duty apply to this service. Controls required under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to this service.

charter:
# Project Charter: Beacon Meadow
Domain: Financial Services. Business unit: Treasury Operations. Initiative type: data platform migration.
## Purpose
The purpose of Beacon Meadow is to decommission the legacy store behind the mortgage origination journey after a controlled migration.
## Background
Previous infrastructure changes caused two major incidents, so change control is under scrutiny. Failures would directly affect operations analysts and be visible to the regulator. Lessons learned from previous initiatives in this area have been reviewed.
## Objectives
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.5 out of 5.
* Reduce defect escape rate by 23 percent compared with the previous release.
* Cut operational cost of the mortgage origination journey by 14 percent.
## Scope
In scope: the mortgage origination journey and the processes used by operations analysts.
Out of scope: Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts. Native tablet applications.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 11 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 30 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Treasury Operations. Funding beyond the first phase depends on demonstrated benefits.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Customer identity and financial data flow through the service. Traffic spikes sharply at month end and during marketing events. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
No specific external regulation applies beyond standard corporate policies.

Domain: Retail and Ecommerce. Business unit: Store Systems.
## Purpose
The purpose of Cobalt Lighthouse is to deliver a refreshed loyalty wallet that improves conversion for loyalty members.
## Background
Small increments will be shipped daily and measured in production. Stakeholders include representatives from 10 departments with differing priorities. This is a public channel and must work for people with a wide range of needs. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.

* Retire 8 legacy components by the end of the project.

In scope: the loyalty wallet and the processes used by loyalty members.
Out of scope: Changes to the enterprise identity provider. Replacement of the finance general ledger.

The delivery team comprises 6 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 37 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Store Systems. Training for end users will be coordinated with the change management team.

The service processes about 30,000 transactions per day and outages have immediate customer impact. The system will store personal data including names, contact details and account history. The core scope is understood although some secondary features remain open. The project will report progress to the portfolio board each month.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018.

Domain: Financial Services. Business unit: Markets Technology. Initiative type: regulatory module.
## Purpose
The purpose of Harbour Vector is to implement a credit decisioning engine that satisfies new regulatory obligations.
## Background
An external customer must sign off each release in their own acceptance environment. Small increments will be shipped daily and measured in production. Success will be measured against the benefits profile in the business case.
## Objectives
* Cut operational cost of the credit decisioning engine by 16 percent.
* Retire 5 legacy components by the end of the project.
* Reduce average handling time for small business owners by 17 percent.
## Scope
In scope: the credit decisioning engine and the processes used by small business owners.
Out of scope: Replacement of the finance general ledger. Native tablet applications.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 8 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 34 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Markets Technology. Key risks will be tracked in the project risk register.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Sensitive personal information will be processed and retained under our data policy. The deadline is immovable because it is tied to a regulatory effective date. Documentation will be maintained in the shared knowledge space.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of the FCA Consumer Duty. Compliance with Sarbanes Oxley Section 404 internal controls must be demonstrated before go live.
text:

Workflow archetype adopted: Kanban Continuous Flow. State flow: Intake > Triage > Ready > In Progress > Peer Review > Deploy and Verify > Done.
Workflow adjustments applied: add accessibility review.
Outcome score 0.31 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 44%, defect escape rate 15.0%, median cycle time 13.4 days, stakeholder satisfaction 2.4 out of 5, 6 compliance findings.
The workflow mostly worked although some stages felt either too heavy or too light.
Charter summary follows.

title: Juniper Meadow (trade surveillance dashboard)
charter:
# Project Charter: Juniper Meadow
Domain: Financial Services. Business unit: Lending. Initiative type: infrastructure upgrade.
## Purpose
The purpose of Juniper Meadow is to upgrade the infrastructure behind the trade surveillance dashboard to supported versions.
## Background
Traffic spikes sharply at month end and during marketing events. Any downtime breaches contractual service levels and triggers financial penalties. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.
## Objectives
* Increase digital adoption among operations analysts to 20 percent within a year.
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.6 out of 5.
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the trade surveillance dashboard.
## Scope
In scope: the trade surveillance dashboard and the processes used by operations analysts.
Out of scope: Organisational restructuring of the operations teams. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 5 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 24 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Lending. The team is co located three days a week and remote on other days.
## Constraints and Assumptions
1 teams, including two platform teams, contribute to the same release. Success depends on experiments whose outcomes we cannot predict in advance. Budget has been approved for the current financial year.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Compliance with MiFID II record keeping obligations must be demonstrated before go live.
text:

Workflow archetype adopted: Dual Track Discovery and Delivery. State flow: Opportunity Backlog > Hypothesis Framing > Discovery Research > Experiment Running > Evidence Review > Delivery Backlog > Building > Validation in Production > Learned and Shipped.
Workflow adjustments applied: add data migration rehearsal, add performance test, add security review.
Outcome score 0.76 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 85%, defect escape rate 6.5%, median cycle time 5.4 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.2 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.
The team adapted the lifecycle informally because parts of it did not fit the work.
Charter summary follows.

charter:
# Project Charter: Linden Pathway
Domain: Medical Devices. Business unit: Device Software. Initiative type: data platform migration.
## Purpose
The purpose of Linden Pathway is to move all records held by the insulin dosing companion app onto the strategic data platform.
## Background
All changes require an approved implementation plan and a defined change window. Hardware prototypes arrive in batches, constraining when integration testing can start. The team is co located three days a week and remote on other days.
## Objectives
* Cut operational cost of the insulin dosing companion app by 29 percent.
* Increase digital adoption among hospital biomedical teams to 24 percent within a year.
* Reduce average handling time for hospital biomedical teams by 42 percent.
## Scope
In scope: the insulin dosing companion app and the processes used by hospital biomedical teams.
Out of scope: Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 8 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 22 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Device Software. Lessons learned from previous initiatives in this area have been reviewed.
## Constraints and Assumptions
The work is split across 2 product teams who must integrate continuously. Any downtime breaches contractual service levels and triggers financial penalties. Historical data must be reconciled and migrated before the old system is switched off. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Controls required under FDA 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records and signatures apply to this service. Controls required under IEC 62304 medical device software lifecycle apply to this service. The solution falls within scope of ISO 13485 quality management system.

charter:
# Project Charter: Marble Canopy
Domain: Telecommunications. Business unit: OSS and BSS. Initiative type: machine learning research.
## Purpose
The purpose of Marble Canopy is to establish whether machine learning can improve decisions in the router firmware rollout.
## Background
Predictions will be generated by a trained model that must be monitored for drift. Feasibility is unproven; the first weeks will test several competing hypotheses. Architecture decisions will be recorded and reviewed by the design authority.
## Objectives
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the router firmware rollout.
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.4 out of 5.
* Retire 4 legacy components by the end of the project.
## Scope
In scope: the router firmware rollout and the processes used by retail advisors.
Out of scope: Native tablet applications. Organisational restructuring of the operations teams.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 6 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 11 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within OSS and BSS. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Hardware prototypes arrive in batches, constraining when integration testing can start. Priorities are likely to shift every few weeks as competitor launches are assessed. Success will be measured against the benefits profile in the business case.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Controls required under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to this service. Compliance with ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls must be demonstrated before go live.

Workflow adjustments applied: add model validation, add privacy review, add vendor checkpoint.
Outcome score 0.79 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 82%, defect escape rate 5.6%, median cycle time 5.6 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.1 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.

Charter summary follows.

Domain: Energy and Utilities. Business unit: Customer Billing.
## Purpose
The purpose of Obsidian Quarry 896 is to replace the ageing demand forecasting service with a modern responsive application for field engineers.
## Background
The team deploys to production several times per day behind feature flags. Peak load is forecast at 7600 requests per second during seasonal campaigns. Some interrupt work is expected from the existing product while the new features are built. The project will report progress to the portfolio board each month.
## Objectives
* Cut operational cost of the demand forecasting service by 22 percent.
* Retire 2 legacy components by the end of the project.
* Increase digital adoption among field engineers to 12 percent within a year.
## Scope
In scope: the demand forecasting service and the processes used by field engineers.
Out of scope: Changes to the enterprise identity provider. Organisational restructuring of the operations teams.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 5 people organised into 1 team. The sponsor sits within Customer Billing. Funding beyond the first phase depends on demonstrated benefits.
## Constraints and Assumptions
This is a public channel and must work for people with a wide range of needs. Requirements are expected to evolve as we learn from early customer feedback. Sensitive personal information will be processed and retained under our data policy. Success will be measured against the benefits profile in the business case.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of the NIS2 Directive.

Workflow archetype adopted: Agile Scrum Product Delivery. State flow: Product Backlog > Sprint Backlog > In Progress > Code Review > QA Verification > Ready for Release > Done.
Workflow adjustments applied: add feature flags.
Outcome score 0.78 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 89%, defect escape rate 5.8%, median cycle time 7.5 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.2 out of 5, 1 compliance findings.
Flow through the workflow was smooth and predictable for most of the project.
Charter summary follows.

title: Tidal Prism (claims triage service)
charter:
# Project Charter: Tidal Prism
Domain: Insurance. Business unit: Broker Channels. Initiative type: infrastructure upgrade.
## Purpose
The purpose of Tidal Prism is to replace end of life hosting for the claims triage service without customer disruption.
## Background
Changes after tooling is cut are extremely expensive, so design decisions must be frozen early. Changes to production must respect the quarterly change freeze and the weekly change advisory board. Budget has been approved for the current financial year.
## Objectives
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the claims triage service.
* Reduce defect escape rate by 16 percent compared with the previous release.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
## Scope
In scope: the claims triage service and the processes used by policyholders.
Out of scope: Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 8 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 18 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Broker Channels. Training for end users will be coordinated with the change management team.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Any downtime breaches contractual service levels and triggers financial penalties. Traffic spikes sharply at month end and during marketing events. The deadline is immovable because it is tied to a regulatory effective date. Architecture decisions will be recorded and reviewed by the design authority.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Compliance with the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act must be demonstrated before go live. Compliance with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 must be demonstrated before go live. The solution falls within scope of ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP00948: Tidal Prism (claims triage service).
Workflow archetype adopted: Change Controlled Operations. State flow: Change Request > Risk Assessment > Change Advisory Board Review > Scheduled > Implementing > Post Implementation Review > Closed.
Workflow adjustments applied: add performance test, add rollback plan, add security review.
Outcome score 0.92 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 87%, defect escape rate 2.5%, median cycle time 3.5 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.4 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.
The lifecycle suited the problem; ceremonies and gates felt proportionate rather than bureaucratic.
Charter summary follows.

charter:
# Project Charter: Granite Vector 900
Domain: Public Sector. Business unit: Local Government.
## Purpose
The purpose of Granite Vector 900 is to migrate the citizen account service from the legacy data centre to the cloud platform.
## Background
An external vendor supplies a core component under a fixed price contract. Sensitive personal information will be processed and retained under our data policy. All changes require an approved implementation plan and a defined change window. caseworkers will access the service from their own devices without assistance. Architecture decisions will be recorded and reviewed by the design authority.
## Objectives
* Increase digital adoption among caseworkers to 14 percent within a year.
* Reduce average handling time for caseworkers by 25 percent.
* Reduce defect escape rate by 11 percent compared with the previous release.
## Scope
In scope: the citizen account service and the processes used by caseworkers.
Out of scope: Changes to the enterprise identity provider. Organisational restructuring of the operations teams.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 6 people organised into 3 teams. The planned duration is 42 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Local Government. The product owner has authority to make day to day scope decisions within agreed tolerances.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Traffic spikes sharply at month end and during marketing events. Historical data must be reconciled and migrated before the old system is switched off. Failures would directly affect caseworkers and be visible to the regulator. Requirements are stable and fully specified in the approved requirements catalogue. Success will be measured against the benefits profile in the business case.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Controls required under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to this service. Compliance with WCAG 2.2 AA and the Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations must be demonstrated before go live.

charter:
# Project Charter: Obsidian Sentinel 900
Domain: Public Sector. Business unit: Digital Services. Initiative type: machine learning research.
## Purpose
The purpose of Obsidian Sentinel 900 is to prototype predictive models that could power the court booking system.
## Background
Acceptance by the commissioning client is a contractual requirement. A machine learning model will score cases and route them to the right queue. The service processes about 430,000 transactions per day and outages have immediate customer impact. The team is co located three days a week and remote on other days.
## Objectives
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Cut operational cost of the court booking system by 29 percent.
* Increase digital adoption among council officers to 20 percent within a year.
## Scope
In scope: the court booking system and the processes used by council officers.
Out of scope: Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts. Native tablet applications.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 6 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 10 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Digital Services. Funding beyond the first phase depends on demonstrated benefits.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Some interrupt work is expected from the existing product while the new features are built. We do not yet know which capabilities will matter most, so the scope will be shaped by usage data. The system will store personal data including names, contact details and account history. It is not yet clear that the available data supports a reliable solution. The team will share a dashboard of delivery metrics with sponsors.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Compliance with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 must be demonstrated before go live.

Domain: Energy and Utilities. Business unit: Grid Operations. Initiative type: internal tooling.
## Purpose
The purpose of Saffron Mosaic 900 is to give asset managers a self service field workforce scheduler to replace email requests.
## Background
The team will balance roadmap items with a moderate volume of operational requests. Budget has been approved for the current financial year.
## Objectives
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.6 out of 5.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Increase digital adoption among asset managers to 10 percent within a year.
## Scope
In scope: the field workforce scheduler and the processes used by asset managers.
Out of scope: Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts. Organisational restructuring of the operations teams.
## Team and Stakeholders
The planned duration is 15 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Grid Operations. Key risks will be tracked in the project risk register.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Requirements are expected to evolve as we learn from early customer feedback. Customer identity and financial data flow through the service. Funding beyond the first phase depends on demonstrated benefits.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Controls required under the NIS2 Directive apply to this service.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP01440: Saffron Mosaic 900 (field workforce scheduler).
Workflow archetype adopted: Agile Scrum Product Delivery. State flow: Product Backlog > Sprint Backlog > In Progress > Code Review > QA Verification > Ready for Release > Done.
Workflow adjustments applied: add uat stage.
Outcome score 0.63 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 62%, defect escape rate 8.9%, median cycle time 8.0 days, stakeholder satisfaction 3.5 out of 5, 3 compliance findings.
The chosen workflow matched the nature of the work and the team settled into a steady rhythm.
Charter summary follows.

charter:
# Project Charter: Nimbus Orbit 900
Domain: Telecommunications. Business unit: OSS and BSS.
## Purpose
The purpose of Nimbus Orbit 900 is to certify and roll out new firmware for the network inventory system across the installed base.
## Background
An external customer must sign off each release in their own acceptance environment. Documentation will be maintained in the shared knowledge space.
## Objectives
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the network inventory system.
* Increase digital adoption among retail advisors to 21 percent within a year.
## Scope
In scope: the network inventory system and the processes used by retail advisors.
Out of scope: Replacement of the finance general ledger. Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 15 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 67 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within OSS and BSS. Funding beyond the first phase depends on demonstrated benefits.

The service will be used directly by members of the public. Changes after tooling is cut are extremely expensive, so design decisions must be frozen early. Lessons learned from previous initiatives in this area have been reviewed.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. The solution falls within scope of ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls.

title: Sterling Citadel 900 (claims triage service)
charter:
# Project Charter: Sterling Citadel 900
Domain: Insurance. Business unit: Claims. Initiative type: machine learning research.
## Purpose
The purpose of Sterling Citadel 900 is to investigate data driven approaches to automate the claims triage service.
## Background
A machine learning model will score cases and route them to the right queue. The product owner has authority to make day to day scope decisions within agreed tolerances.
## Objectives
* Increase digital adoption among brokers to 13 percent within a year.
* Reduce defect escape rate by 28 percent compared with the previous release.
* Retire 2 legacy components by the end of the project.
## Scope
In scope: the claims triage service and the processes used by brokers.
Out of scope: Replacement of the finance general ledger. Organisational restructuring of the operations teams.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 5 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 26 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Claims. The project will report progress to the portfolio board each month.
## Constraints and Assumptions
We must establish quickly whether the approach works before committing to a full build. Priorities are likely to shift every few weeks as competitor launches are assessed. Architecture decisions will be recorded and reviewed by the design authority.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
No specific external regulation applies beyond standard corporate policies.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP01444: Sterling Citadel 900 (claims triage service).
Workflow archetype adopted: Dual Track Discovery and Delivery. State flow: Opportunity Backlog > Hypothesis Framing > Discovery Research > Experiment Running > Evidence Review > Delivery Backlog > Building > Validation in Production > Learned and Shipped.
Workflow adjustments applied: add definition of ready, add spike timebox.
Outcome score 0.82 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 80%, defect escape rate 5.3%, median cycle time 7.1 days, stakeholder satisfaction 4.4 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.
Flow through the workflow was smooth and predictable for most of the project.
Charter summary follows.

Priorities are likely to shift every few weeks as competitor launches are assessed. An external vendor supplies a core component under a fixed price contract. The project will report progress to the portfolio board each month.
