# Project Charter: Coastal Quarry 900
Domain: Healthcare Provision. Business unit: Digital Health. Initiative type: customer facing application.
## Purpose
The purpose of Coastal Quarry 900 is to replace the ageing clinical referral pathway with a modern responsive application for care coordinators.
## Background
The team will balance roadmap items with a moderate volume of operational requests. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Objectives
* Increase digital adoption among care coordinators to 38 percent within a year.
* Reduce defect escape rate by 36 percent compared with the previous release.
* Retire 3 legacy components by the end of the project.
## Scope
In scope: the clinical referral pathway and the processes used by care coordinators.
Out of scope: Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 7 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 33 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Digital Health. The product owner has authority to make day to day scope decisions within agreed tolerances.
## Constraints and Assumptions
The system will store personal data including names, contact details and account history. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Controls required under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to this service. Controls required under HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules apply to this service.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP01509: Coastal Quarry 900 (clinical referral pathway).
Workflow archetype adopted: Agile Scrum Product Delivery. State flow: Product Backlog > Sprint Backlog > In Progress > Code Review > QA Verification > Ready for Release > Done.
Workflow adjustments applied: none.
Outcome score 0.39 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 50%, defect escape rate 12.4%, median cycle time 11.0 days, stakeholder satisfaction 2.5 out of 5, 2 compliance findings.
Predictability was acceptable, but the process needed several mid course corrections.
Charter summary follows.

title: Beacon Lattice 900 (live events ticketing app)
charter:
# Project Charter: Beacon Lattice 900
Domain: Media and Entertainment. Business unit: Audience Data. Initiative type: new product feature.
## Purpose
The purpose of Beacon Lattice 900 is to launch a live events ticketing app that differentiates our proposition for content editors.
## Background
Much of the detail will emerge through prototypes reviewed with real users. Historical data must be reconciled and migrated before the old system is switched off. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.
## Objectives
* Reduce defect escape rate by 21 percent compared with the previous release.
* Increase digital adoption among content editors to 24 percent within a year.
* Retire 4 legacy components by the end of the project.
## Scope
In scope: the live events ticketing app and the processes used by content editors.
Out of scope: Changes to the enterprise identity provider. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 5 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 32 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Audience Data. Training for end users will be coordinated with the change management team.
## Constraints and Assumptions
The service must scale to several million sessions on launch day. Stakeholders include representatives from 5 departments with differing priorities. content editors will access the service from their own devices without assistance. Funding beyond the first phase depends on demonstrated benefits.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of PCI DSS v4.0.

charter:
# Project Charter: Meridian Sentinel 900
Domain: Insurance. Business unit: Policy Administration. Initiative type: regulatory module.
## Purpose
The purpose of Meridian Sentinel 900 is to implement a underwriting workbench that satisfies new regulatory obligations.
## Background
Stakeholders include representatives from 5 departments with differing priorities. Funding beyond the first phase depends on demonstrated benefits.
## Objectives
* Retire 2 legacy components by the end of the project.
* Increase digital adoption among claims handlers to 36 percent within a year.
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the underwriting workbench.
## Scope
In scope: the underwriting workbench and the processes used by claims handlers.
Out of scope: Changes to the enterprise identity provider. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 9 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 50 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Policy Administration. Key risks will be tracked in the project risk register.

charter:
# Project Charter: Pioneer Beacon 900
Domain: Manufacturing. Business unit: Industrial IoT.
## Purpose
The purpose of Pioneer Beacon 900 is to launch a production scheduling engine that differentiates our proposition for maintenance engineers.
## Background
The client will formally accept deliverables before payment milestones are released. Customer identity and financial data flow through the service. The service will be used directly by members of the public. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.
## Objectives
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.0 out of 5.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Cut operational cost of the production scheduling engine by 44 percent.
## Scope
In scope: the production scheduling engine and the processes used by maintenance engineers.
Out of scope: Organisational restructuring of the operations teams. Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 7 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 34 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Industrial IoT. Architecture decisions will be recorded and reviewed by the design authority.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Priorities are likely to shift every few weeks as competitor launches are assessed. Traffic spikes sharply at month end and during marketing events. The work is split across 1 product teams who must integrate continuously. Funding beyond the first phase depends on demonstrated benefits.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
There are no sector specific regulatory requirements for this work.

Domain: Public Sector. Business unit: Benefits Delivery. Initiative type: infrastructure upgrade.
## Purpose
The purpose of Orchard Cascade 900 is to harden the network and compute estate supporting the licensing application service.
## Background
All changes require an approved implementation plan and a defined change window. Budget has been approved for the current financial year.
## Objectives
* Reduce defect escape rate by 12 percent compared with the previous release.
* Retire 5 legacy components by the end of the project.
* Reduce average handling time for caseworkers by 27 percent.
## Scope
In scope: the licensing application service and the processes used by caseworkers.
Out of scope: Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 4 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 10 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Benefits Delivery. Documentation will be maintained in the shared knowledge space.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Requirements are stable and fully specified in the approved requirements catalogue. Delivery depends on milestones from our technology partner. Success will be measured against the benefits profile in the business case.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
No specific external regulation applies beyond standard corporate policies.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP01617: Orchard Cascade 900 (licensing application service).
Workflow archetype adopted: Change Controlled Operations. State flow: Change Request > Risk Assessment > Change Advisory Board Review > Scheduled > Implementing > Post Implementation Review > Closed.
Workflow adjustments applied: none.
Outcome score 0.70 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 72%, defect escape rate 7.4%, median cycle time 7.2 days, stakeholder satisfaction 3.7 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.
Flow through the workflow was smooth and predictable for most of the project.
Charter summary follows.

# Project Charter: Falcon Quarry 900
Domain: Education. Business unit: Research Computing. Initiative type: new product feature.
## Purpose
The purpose of Falcon Quarry 900 is to build the first release of a student enrolment portal for students.

Priorities are likely to shift every few weeks as competitor launches are assessed. Training for end users will be coordinated with the change management team.
## Objectives
* Retire 2 legacy components by the end of the project.
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.1 out of 5.

In scope: the student enrolment portal and the processes used by students.
Out of scope: Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts. Replacement of the finance general ledger.

The delivery team comprises 9 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 36 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Research Computing. Architecture decisions will be recorded and reviewed by the design authority.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Several business owners share accountability for outcomes. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018.

The lifecycle suited the problem; ceremonies and gates felt proportionate rather than bureaucratic.
Charter summary follows.

charter:
# Project Charter: Linden Keystone 900
Domain: Manufacturing. Business unit: Product Engineering. Initiative type: regulatory module.
## Purpose
The purpose of Linden Keystone 900 is to introduce controls in the supplier portal that close audit findings.
## Background
Little change is expected because the functional design was agreed in detail with all parties. Architecture decisions will be recorded and reviewed by the design authority.
## Objectives
* Reduce average handling time for quality inspectors by 39 percent.
* Cut operational cost of the supplier portal by 28 percent.
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the supplier portal.
## Scope
In scope: the supplier portal and the processes used by quality inspectors.
Out of scope: Replacement of the finance general ledger. Native tablet applications.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 12 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 39 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Product Engineering. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Several business owners share accountability for outcomes. Peak load is forecast at 2900 requests per second during seasonal campaigns. Success will be measured against the benefits profile in the business case.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Compliance with Sarbanes Oxley Section 404 internal controls must be demonstrated before go live.

title: Atlas Cascade 900 (demand forecasting service)
charter:
# Project Charter: Atlas Cascade 900
Domain: Energy and Utilities. Business unit: Smart Metering. Initiative type: hardware and firmware.
## Purpose
The purpose of Atlas Cascade 900 is to deliver a firmware release for the demand forecasting service that ships with the next hardware revision.
## Background
An external vendor supplies a core component under a fixed price contract. Firmware must be validated on physical devices before field deployment. Demand is interrupt driven, with priority one incidents expected to be picked up within the hour. Training for end users will be coordinated with the change management team.
## Objectives
* Reduce average handling time for grid controllers by 22 percent.
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.5 out of 5.
* Cut operational cost of the demand forecasting service by 14 percent.
## Scope
In scope: the demand forecasting service and the processes used by grid controllers.
Out of scope: Changes to the enterprise identity provider. Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 6 people organised into 3 teams. The planned duration is 41 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Smart Metering. The team will share a dashboard of delivery metrics with sponsors.
## Constraints and Assumptions
The deadline is immovable because it is tied to a regulatory effective date. An external customer must sign off each release in their own acceptance environment. The specification was baselined last quarter and changes require formal approval. The project will report progress to the portfolio board each month.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Controls required under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to this service. Controls required under ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls apply to this service. Compliance with the NIS2 Directive must be demonstrated before go live.

Flow through the workflow was smooth and predictable for most of the project.

# Project Charter: Tidal Beacon 900
Domain: Retail and Ecommerce. Business unit: Supply Chain Technology.
## Purpose
The purpose of Tidal Beacon 900 is to deliver a click and collect service that lets online shoppers complete key tasks without contacting support.
## Background
Small increments will be shipped daily and measured in production. The product owner has authority to make day to day scope decisions within agreed tolerances.
## Objectives
* Cut operational cost of the click and collect service by 15 percent.
* Reduce defect escape rate by 40 percent compared with the previous release.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
## Scope
In scope: the click and collect service and the processes used by online shoppers.
Out of scope: Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts. Changes to the enterprise identity provider.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 5 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 22 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Supply Chain Technology. The team will share a dashboard of delivery metrics with sponsors.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Sensitive personal information will be processed and retained under our data policy. A broad stakeholder group must stay informed, including executive sponsors and frontline managers. Key risks will be tracked in the project risk register.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of PCI DSS v4.0. The solution falls within scope of WCAG 2.2 AA and the Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP01676: Tidal Beacon 900 (click and collect service).
Workflow archetype adopted: Agile Scrum Product Delivery. State flow: Product Backlog > Sprint Backlog > In Progress > Code Review > QA Verification > Ready for Release > Done.
Workflow adjustments applied: tighten wip.
Outcome score 0.73 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 88%, defect escape rate 5.9%, median cycle time 7.3 days, stakeholder satisfaction 3.8 out of 5, 1 compliance findings.
Flow through the workflow was smooth and predictable for most of the project.
Charter summary follows.

title: Vantage Pathway 900 (underwriting workbench)
charter:
# Project Charter: Vantage Pathway 900
Domain: Insurance. Business unit: Underwriting. Initiative type: machine learning research.
## Purpose
The purpose of Vantage Pathway 900 is to prototype predictive models that could power the underwriting workbench.
## Background
Hardware prototypes arrive in batches, constraining when integration testing can start. Lessons learned from previous initiatives in this area have been reviewed.
## Objectives
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the underwriting workbench.
* Retire 4 legacy components by the end of the project.
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.0 out of 5.
## Scope
In scope: the underwriting workbench and the processes used by brokers.
Out of scope: Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 7 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 27 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Underwriting. Success will be measured against the benefits profile in the business case.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Much of the detail will emerge through prototypes reviewed with real users. Predictions will be generated by a trained model that must be monitored for drift. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
The solution falls within scope of the FCA Consumer Duty.

## Purpose
The purpose of Meridian Meadow 900 is to prototype predictive models that could power the demand forecasting service.

* Reduce average handling time for grid controllers by 21 percent.
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.2 out of 5.
* Cut operational cost of the demand forecasting service by 33 percent.

The delivery team comprises 7 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 21 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Grid Operations. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.

Requirements are expected to evolve as we learn from early customer feedback. The deadline is immovable because it is tied to a regulatory effective date. Documentation will be maintained in the shared knowledge space.

The solution falls within scope of UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. Compliance with the NIS2 Directive must be demonstrated before go live.

# Project Charter: Nimbus Quarry 900
Domain: Financial Services. Business unit: Lending.

Domain: Energy and Utilities. Business unit: Smart Metering. Initiative type: new product feature.
## Purpose
The purpose of Quartz Cascade 900 is to launch a asset condition monitoring that differentiates our proposition for domestic customers.
## Background
A broad stakeholder group must stay informed, including executive sponsors and frontline managers. Customer identity and financial data flow through the service. The project will report progress to the portfolio board each month.
## Objectives
* Deliver measurable improvement in the main business metric for the asset condition monitoring.
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.6 out of 5.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
## Scope
In scope: the asset condition monitoring and the processes used by domestic customers.
Out of scope: Organisational restructuring of the operations teams. Changes to third party contracts beyond those listed.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 9 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 26 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Smart Metering. Budget has been approved for the current financial year.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Contractual penalties apply if the delivery date is missed. We must establish quickly whether the approach works before committing to a full build. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
No specific external regulation applies beyond standard corporate policies.
text:
Historical project blueprint BP01822: Quartz Cascade 900 (asset condition monitoring).
Workflow archetype adopted: Regulated Compliance Pipeline. State flow: Draft Requirement > Requirements Traceability > Design Review > Implementation > Verification > Independent Validation > Compliance Review > Release Authorisation > Released.
Workflow adjustments applied: none.
Outcome score 0.42 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 54%, defect escape rate 12.6%, median cycle time 10.5 days, stakeholder satisfaction 2.7 out of 5, 1 compliance findings.
The workflow mostly worked although some stages felt either too heavy or too light.
Charter summary follows.

title: Quiet Gateway 900 (predictive maintenance service)
charter:
# Project Charter: Quiet Gateway 900
Domain: Manufacturing. Business unit: Quality Engineering. Initiative type: hardware and firmware.
## Purpose
The purpose of Quiet Gateway 900 is to co develop the predictive maintenance service with our hardware partner for field deployment.
## Background
The deadline is immovable because it is tied to a regulatory effective date. The team is co located three days a week and remote on other days.
## Objectives
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.4 out of 5.
* Cut operational cost of the predictive maintenance service by 24 percent.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
## Scope
In scope: the predictive maintenance service and the processes used by maintenance engineers.
Out of scope: Native tablet applications. Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 14 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 52 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Quality Engineering. The team will share a dashboard of delivery metrics with sponsors.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Most requirements are known, with a handful expected to change after the first release. Requirements are stable and fully specified in the approved requirements catalogue. The product owner has authority to make day to day scope decisions within agreed tolerances.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
No specific external regulation applies beyond standard corporate policies.

Workflow adjustments applied: add definition of ready, add vendor checkpoint.
Outcome score 0.67 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 66%, defect escape rate 7.2%, median cycle time 8.7 days, stakeholder satisfaction 3.5 out of 5, 0 compliance findings.
The chosen workflow matched the nature of the work and the team settled into a steady rhythm.
Charter summary follows.

# Project Charter: Linden Current 900
Domain: Pharmaceuticals and Life Sciences. Business unit: Pharmacovigilance. Initiative type: internal tooling.
## Purpose
The purpose of Linden Current 900 is to build an internal stability study tracker that removes manual spreadsheet work for pharmacovigilance scientists.
## Background
The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Objectives
* Increase digital adoption among pharmacovigilance scientists to 44 percent within a year.
* Retire 4 legacy components by the end of the project.
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.2 out of 5.
## Scope
In scope: the stability study tracker and the processes used by pharmacovigilance scientists.
Out of scope: Replacement of the finance general ledger. Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 3 people organised into 1 team. The planned duration is 24 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Pharmacovigilance. Success will be measured against the benefits profile in the business case.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Lessons learned from previous initiatives in this area have been reviewed.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Compliance with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 must be demonstrated before go live. Compliance with ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls must be demonstrated before go live.

Workflow adjustments applied: add privacy review.
Outcome score 0.58 on a zero to one scale. On time delivery 65%, defect escape rate 10.3%, median cycle time 8.0 days, stakeholder satisfaction 3.7 out of 5, 2 compliance findings.

charter:
# Project Charter: Harbour Signal 900
Domain: Education. Business unit: Learning Technology.
## Purpose
The purpose of Harbour Signal 900 is to investigate data driven approaches to automate the timetabling service.
## Background
Historical data must be reconciled and migrated before the old system is switched off. Feasibility is unproven; the first weeks will test several competing hypotheses. Success will be measured against the benefits profile in the business case.
## Objectives
* Retire 3 legacy components by the end of the project.
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.2 out of 5.
* Increase digital adoption among admissions officers to 26 percent within a year.
## Scope
In scope: the timetabling service and the processes used by admissions officers.
Out of scope: Organisational restructuring of the operations teams. Native tablet applications.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 6 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 12 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Learning Technology. The team is co located three days a week and remote on other days.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Most requirements are known, with a handful expected to change after the first release. Requirements are expected to evolve as we learn from early customer feedback. The solution relies on a classification model trained on historical outcomes. The project will report progress to the portfolio board each month.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Controls required under WCAG 2.2 AA and the Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations apply to this service.

Charter summary follows.

charter:
# Project Charter: Juniper Canopy 900
Domain: Logistics and Transport. Business unit: Customer Delivery.
## Purpose
The purpose of Juniper Canopy 900 is to migrate the carrier integration hub from the legacy data centre to the cloud platform.
## Background
The team handles a steady stream of incidents and service requests that arrive without notice. Success depends on experiments whose outcomes we cannot predict in advance. Changes to production must respect the quarterly change freeze and the weekly change advisory board. The team will use the standard engineering toolchain and cloud landing zone.
## Objectives
* Reduce average handling time for warehouse operatives by 22 percent.
* Cut operational cost of the carrier integration hub by 38 percent.
* Achieve a customer satisfaction score above 4.4 out of 5.
## Scope
In scope: the carrier integration hub and the processes used by warehouse operatives.
Out of scope: Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts. Native tablet applications.

The delivery team comprises 5 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 22 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Customer Delivery. Budget has been approved for the current financial year.
## Constraints and Assumptions
Scope has been contractually fixed and signed off by the steering committee. The work includes migrating approximately 26 million records from the legacy platform. # Project Charter: Copper Vector 900
Domain: Healthcare Provision. Business unit: Digital Health.
## Purpose
The purpose of Copper Vector 900 is to replace the ageing discharge summary tool with a modern responsive application for ward nurses.
## Background
Customer identity and financial data flow through the service. Priorities are likely to shift every few weeks as competitor launches are assessed. We release continuously through an automated pipeline with progressive rollout. The product owner has authority to make day to day scope decisions within agreed tolerances.
## Objectives
* Cut operational cost of the discharge summary tool by 11 percent.
* Provide auditable evidence that obligations are met for every release.
* Reduce defect escape rate by 17 percent compared with the previous release.
## Scope
In scope: the discharge summary tool and the processes used by ward nurses.
Out of scope: Data warehouse reporting beyond the agreed operational extracts. Replacement of the finance general ledger.
## Team and Stakeholders
The delivery team comprises 12 people organised into 2 teams. The planned duration is 19 weeks from mobilisation. The sponsor sits within Digital Health. The service will follow the enterprise logging and monitoring standards.
## Constraints and Assumptions
The service must scale to several million sessions on launch day. ward nurses will access the service from their own devices without assistance. The platform is classified as a critical service with a recovery time objective of 60 minutes. Success will be measured against the benefits profile in the business case.
## Regulatory and Compliance Context
Controls required under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to this service.
